description: Set up multi-channel alert routing: define alert categories, map each to delivery channels, configure escalation rules, set quiet hours, test the routing, and produce the routing setup document.

steps.description: Define the alert categories and their severity levels for the organization.

inputs.name: systems-inventory
inputs.desc: List of systems and services that produce alerts

inputs.name: team-structure
inputs.desc: Teams and roles responsible for responding to alerts

outputs.name: alert-categories
outputs.desc: Defined categories (critical, warning, informational) with criteria for each

outputs.name: severity-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix mapping alert types to severity levels

process: List every system and service that produces alerts, grouped by function.
Define three to five severity levels with clear criteria for each (impact scope, urgency, customer visibility).
Assign each alert type from the systems inventory to a severity level.
Document the severity matrix with examples for each level.

steps.description: Map each alert category to its delivery channels and recipients.

inputs.name: alert-categories
inputs.desc: Defined alert categories and severity levels

inputs.name: severity-matrix
inputs.desc: Matrix of alert types to severity

outputs.name: channel-map
outputs.desc: Mapping of each category to delivery channels (SMS, email, push, Slack, PagerDuty, phone call)

outputs.name: recipient-roster
outputs.desc: List of recipients for each channel and category

process: For each severity level, select the appropriate channels (critical: phone + SMS + PagerDuty; warning: Slack + email; informational: email or dashboard only).
Assign recipients to each channel based on team structure and on-call rotation.
Document the channel map with fallback channels if the primary is unreachable.
Verify that every alert category has at least one channel and one recipient.

steps.description: Configure escalation rules for unacknowledged alerts.

outputs.name: escalation-rules
outputs.desc: Rules defining when and how to escalate unacknowledged alerts

outputs.name: escalation-contacts
outputs.desc: Ordered list of escalation contacts for each tier

process: Define the acknowledgment window for each severity level (critical: 5 minutes, warning: 30 minutes, informational: none).
Set the escalation path: if no acknowledgment within the window, notify the next tier.
Define three tiers of escalation (primary responder, team lead, management).
Document the override rules for after-hours and weekends.

steps.description: Configure quiet hours and the override rules that bypass them for critical alerts.

outputs.name: quiet-hours-config
outputs.desc: Quiet hours schedule and override rules

outputs.name: override-criteria
outputs.desc: Criteria that cause an alert to bypass quiet hours

process: Define quiet hours for each team or timezone (e.g., 10 PM to 7 AM local).
Specify which severity levels are suppressed during quiet hours (informational, warning).
Define the override criteria: critical alerts always ring through, customer-facing outages always ring through.
Document the configuration so on-call staff know what will and will not wake them.

steps.description: Test the alert routing configuration end to end.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results of routing tests for each severity and channel combination

outputs.name: routing-setup-document
outputs.desc: Final alert routing setup document with all configurations

process: Send a test alert at each severity level and verify it arrives on the correct channel to the correct recipient.
Test the escalation path by letting a test alert go unacknowledged and verifying the escalation fires.
Test quiet hours by sending a non-critical alert during quiet hours and verifying suppression.
Test the override by sending a critical alert during quiet hours and verifying delivery.
Compile the test results and finalize the routing setup document.

description: Manage on-call rotations and handoffs: define the rotation schedule, document the handoff checklist, conduct the handoff, verify contact info, and produce the handoff record.

steps.description: Design the on-call rotation schedule for the team.

inputs.name: team-roster
inputs.desc: List of team members available for on-call

inputs.name: service-coverage-requirements
inputs.desc: Hours and services that require on-call coverage

outputs.name: rotation-schedule
outputs.desc: On-call rotation schedule (weekly, daily, or follow-the-sun)

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Any gaps in coverage and how they are handled

process: Determine the rotation cadence (weekly is standard; daily for high-volume; follow-the-sun for global teams).
Assign team members to rotation slots, balancing weekday and weekend shifts.
Identify coverage gaps (holidays, vacations, single points of failure) and assign backups.
Publish the schedule to the paging system and team calendar.

steps.description: Build the handoff checklist that outgoing on-call completes before transferring to the next person.

outputs.name: handoff-checklist
outputs.desc: Checklist of items to cover during handoff (open incidents, known issues, upcoming changes)

outputs.name: handoff-template
outputs.desc: Template document for recording each handoff

process: List the mandatory handoff items: open incidents and their status, known issues being monitored, upcoming deployments or changes, any pending customer escalations.
Define the format (async written handoff in Slack or wiki, or synchronous 15-minute call).
Create the handoff template with fields for each item.
Set the deadline for completing the handoff (at least 1 hour before rotation ends).

steps.description: Conduct the on-call handoff between the outgoing and incoming responders.

outputs.name: handoff-record
outputs.desc: Completed handoff record with all items addressed

outputs.name: action-items
outputs.desc: Any follow-up actions for the incoming on-call

process: The outgoing on-call fills in the handoff template with current status for each item.
The incoming on-call reviews the template and asks clarifying questions.
Both confirm the handoff is complete and the incoming on-call is now primary.
Log the handoff record in the team's knowledge base.

steps.description: Verify that the incoming on-call's contact information is correct in the paging system.

outputs.name: contact-verification-result
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the paging system has correct contact info

outputs.name: on-call-handoff-report
outputs.desc: Final handoff report with verification status

process: Check that the paging system shows the incoming on-call as the current primary responder.
Send a test page to the incoming on-call and confirm receipt.
Verify the escalation path lists the correct backup contacts.
Record the verification result and close the handoff.

description: Set up and manage a public status page: define monitored components, configure status checks, write communication templates, publish incidents, and produce the management document.

steps.description: Define the components and services displayed on the status page.

inputs.name: service-catalog
inputs.desc: List of services and their dependencies

inputs.name: customer-facing-services
inputs.desc: Which services are visible to customers

outputs.name: component-list
outputs.desc: List of components to display on the status page with grouping

outputs.name: dependency-map
outputs.desc: Map of which components depend on which backend services

process: List every customer-facing service and group them into logical categories (API, web app, mobile, payments, integrations).
Map each component to its backend dependencies so you know what affects what.
Define the status levels for each component (operational, degraded, partial outage, major outage, maintenance).
Decide which internal services are hidden from the public page but tracked internally.

steps.description: Configure automated checks that update the status page based on service health.

inputs.name: component-list
inputs.desc: Components displayed on the status page

outputs.name: check-configuration
outputs.desc: Automated health checks configured for each component

outputs.name: threshold-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for when a check failure triggers a status change

process: For each component, define the health check (HTTP endpoint, synthetic transaction, metric threshold).
Set the check interval (every 1 minute for critical, every 5 minutes for others).
Define the threshold for each status level (e.g., 3 consecutive failures = degraded, 10 = outage).
Configure the integration between the monitoring system and the status page platform.

steps.description: Write the communication templates used during status page incidents.

inputs.name: check-configuration
inputs.desc: Health check setup for each component

outputs.name: incident-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for initial notice, update, and resolution communications

outputs.name: communication-guidelines
outputs.desc: Guidelines for tone, frequency, and content of status updates

process: Write the initial incident template: what is affected, what the impact is, when the next update will be.
Write the update template: what has changed, what the team is doing, when the next update will be.
Write the resolution template: what was affected, what the root cause was, what the team did to fix it.
Document the guidelines: update every 30 minutes during an active incident, use plain language, state facts not guesses.

steps.description: Publish and manage incidents on the status page during an outage.

outputs.name: published-incident-log
outputs.desc: Log of all published incidents and updates

outputs.name: subscriber-notification-record
outputs.desc: Record of notifications sent to status page subscribers

process: When an incident is declared, post the initial notice using the template and set affected components to the correct status.
Post updates at the interval defined in the guidelines (every 30 minutes minimum).
When the incident is resolved, post the resolution notice and return components to operational.
Review the subscriber notification delivery to confirm all subscribers received the updates.

steps.description: Review the status page program and produce the management document.

outputs.name: status-page-metrics
outputs.desc: Metrics on incidents published, update frequency, subscriber count

outputs.name: status-page-management-document
outputs.desc: Final management document with all configurations and processes

process: Review the last quarter's incidents for timeliness and accuracy of updates.
Measure the average time from detection to first status page post.
Check that the component list and health checks are still accurate.
Compile the management document with all configurations, templates, and review findings.

description: Reduce alert fatigue: audit current alerts, classify by signal quality, tune or remove noisy alerts, consolidate related alerts, set up analytics, and produce the reduction report.

steps.description: Audit the current alert volume, frequency, and actionability.

inputs.name: response-logs
inputs.desc: Logs of how each alert was handled (acknowledged, escalated, ignored, auto-resolved)

outputs.name: alert-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of all alert rules with volume and response metrics

outputs.name: noise-candidates
outputs.desc: Alerts flagged as likely noise (high volume, low action rate)

process: Pull the alert history for the last 30 to 90 days grouped by alert rule.
For each rule, calculate the volume, false positive rate, and action rate (percentage that led to a human response).
Flag alerts with an action rate below 10% as noise candidates.
Rank all alerts by noise score (high volume multiplied by low action rate).

steps.description: Classify each alert by criticality and signal quality.

outputs.name: signal-classification
outputs.desc: Each alert classified as high-signal, tunable, or removable

outputs.name: tuning-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific tuning recommendations for each tunable alert

process: Review each noise candidate with the owning team to confirm whether it is truly low-signal.
Classify each alert into three buckets: high-signal (keep as-is), tunable (adjust threshold or consolidate), removable (delete or disable).
For tunable alerts, write the specific recommendation (raise threshold, increase evaluation window, consolidate with a related alert).
For removable alerts, confirm with the owning team before flagging for deletion.

steps.description: Tune or remove noisy alerts based on the classification.

outputs.name: tuning-changelog
outputs.desc: Log of all changes made to alert rules

outputs.name: consolidated-alerts
outputs.desc: List of alerts that were merged or consolidated

process: Apply the tuning recommendations: adjust thresholds, increase evaluation windows, add conditions.
Remove or disable the alerts classified as removable.
Consolidate related alerts that fire together into a single grouped alert.
Log every change in the tuning changelog with the before and after state.

steps.description: Set up ongoing alert analytics to track noise levels over time.

outputs.name: analytics-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard tracking alert volume, action rate, and noise score over time

outputs.name: alert-reduction-report
outputs.desc: Final report documenting the audit, changes, and ongoing metrics

process: Build a dashboard that tracks weekly alert volume, action rate, and noise score by team.
Set a recurring review (monthly) to check for new noise patterns.
Define the target noise level (e.g., action rate above 50% for all alert rules).
Compile the alert reduction report with before-and-after metrics and the analytics setup.

description: Design escalation policies: define tiers, set response time targets, define triggers, configure notification methods, test the paths, and produce the policy document.

steps.description: Define the escalation tiers and the response time targets for each.

inputs.name: service-level-targets
inputs.desc: SLA and SLO response time commitments

outputs.name: tier-definitions
outputs.desc: Defined escalation tiers (L1, L2, L3, management) with roles and responsibilities

outputs.name: response-time-targets
outputs.desc: Response time targets for each tier and severity

process: Define three to four escalation tiers: L1 (first responder, on-call), L2 (subject matter expert), L3 (senior engineer or architect), management (director or VP).
Assign roles and teams to each tier.
Set response time targets: L1 acknowledges within 5 minutes for critical; L2 engaged within 15 minutes if L1 cannot resolve.
Document the responsibilities at each tier (L1 triages and communicates, L2 diagnoses, L3 resolves).

steps.description: Define what triggers an escalation from one tier to the next.

outputs.name: trigger-rules
outputs.desc: Rules that trigger escalation (time-based, severity-based, customer-impact-based)

outputs.name: notification-methods
outputs.desc: How each tier is notified during escalation (page, call, Slack, email)

process: Define time-based triggers: if L1 has not acknowledged in X minutes, escalate to L2.
Define severity-based triggers: critical incidents skip L1 and go directly to L2.
Define customer-impact triggers: if more than N customers are affected, escalate to management immediately.
Map each trigger to the notification method for the receiving tier.

steps.description: Test the escalation paths to verify they work as designed.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results of escalation path tests

outputs.name: escalation-policy-document
outputs.desc: Final escalation policy document with all tiers, triggers, and test results

process: Run a tabletop exercise: simulate a critical incident and walk through the escalation path on paper.
Run a live test: trigger a test alert, let it escalate through the tiers, and verify each notification arrives.
Measure the actual time at each tier against the target response times.
Document any gaps and compile the final escalation policy document.

description: Notify stakeholders during an incident: detect the incident, classify severity, determine the audience, send notifications at defined intervals, and produce the notification record.

steps.description: Classify the incident severity to determine the notification audience and cadence.

inputs.name: incident-details
inputs.desc: Description of the incident (what is affected, when it started, current impact)

inputs.name: severity-criteria
inputs.desc: Criteria for each severity level (SEV1 through SEV4)

outputs.name: severity-level
outputs.desc: Assigned severity level for this incident

outputs.name: notification-audience
outputs.desc: List of stakeholder groups to notify based on severity

process: Evaluate the incident against the severity criteria: customer impact, revenue impact, data integrity, service availability.
Assign the severity level (SEV1: total outage; SEV2: major degradation; SEV3: partial issue; SEV4: minor).
Map the severity to the notification audience (SEV1: all stakeholders including executives; SEV4: engineering only).
Record the classification rationale.

steps.description: Send the initial incident notification to the determined audience.

outputs.name: initial-notification
outputs.desc: The initial notification message sent to stakeholders

outputs.name: delivery-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the notification reached each channel

process: Draft the initial notification: what is affected, what the current impact is, who is investigating, when the next update will be.
Send to each audience group on their designated channel (engineering: Slack; leadership: email + Slack; customers: status page).
Confirm delivery on each channel.
Set the timer for the next update based on severity (SEV1: every 15 minutes; SEV2: every 30 minutes).

steps.description: Send periodic updates at the defined cadence throughout the incident.

outputs.name: update-log
outputs.desc: Log of all periodic updates sent during the incident

outputs.name: stakeholder-questions
outputs.desc: Questions or requests received from stakeholders during the incident

process: At each update interval, gather the latest status from the incident commander.
Draft the update: what has changed, what the team is doing now, what the estimated time to resolution is.
Send the update to all channels and confirm delivery.
Log the update and note any stakeholder questions that need follow-up.

steps.description: Send the resolution notification and produce the notification record.

outputs.name: resolution-notice
outputs.desc: The resolution notification sent to all stakeholders

outputs.name: incident-notification-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of all notifications sent during this incident

process: Draft the resolution notice: what was affected, what the root cause was, what fixed it, whether any follow-up is needed.
Send to all channels and confirm delivery.
Answer any outstanding stakeholder questions.
Compile the full notification record (initial, updates, resolution) with timestamps and delivery confirmations.

description: Automate scheduled report distribution: inventory reports and recipients, define the schedule, configure generation, set up distribution, handle failures, and produce the setup document.

steps.description: Inventory all recurring reports and their current recipients.

inputs.name: department-list
inputs.desc: List of departments that receive recurring reports

inputs.name: current-reports
inputs.desc: Known recurring reports and their delivery methods

outputs.name: report-catalog
outputs.desc: Catalog of all recurring reports with frequency, recipients, data sources, and format

outputs.name: automation-candidates
outputs.desc: Reports that are currently manual and could be automated

process: Survey each department to identify all recurring reports they produce or receive.
For each report, record: name, frequency, recipients, data source, current delivery method, format.
Flag reports that are produced manually as automation candidates.
Flag reports with overlapping content for potential consolidation.

steps.description: Define the generation and distribution schedule for each report.

outputs.name: report-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for each report (generation time, distribution time, timezone)

outputs.name: data-source-map
outputs.desc: Map of each report to its data source and query

process: Set the generation time for each report (allow enough lead time for data to be complete).
Set the distribution time (recipients expect the report by a specific hour).
Map each report to its data source and the query or pipeline that produces it.
Handle timezone differences for global teams.

steps.description: Configure the automated report generation pipeline.

outputs.name: generation-config
outputs.desc: Configuration for the automated report generation system

outputs.name: output-format-specs
outputs.desc: Format specifications for each report (PDF, CSV, dashboard link)

process: For each report, configure the data query to run at the scheduled generation time.
Define the output format (PDF for executives, CSV for analysts, dashboard link for teams).
Set up the generation pipeline: query, transform, render, store.
Add validation checks to flag reports with missing or anomalous data before distribution.

steps.description: Set up the distribution channels and handle delivery failures.

outputs.name: distribution-config
outputs.desc: Distribution configuration (channels, recipients, retry logic)

outputs.name: report-distribution-document
outputs.desc: Final setup document covering schedule, generation, and distribution

process: Configure the delivery channel for each report (email, Slack, shared drive, dashboard).
Set up retry logic for failed deliveries (retry once after 15 minutes, then alert the report owner).
Add a delivery confirmation log so the team can verify reports were received.
Compile the final setup document with the full schedule, generation config, and distribution config.

description: Configure threshold-based alerts for business metrics: define the metrics, set thresholds, configure channels, set cool-down periods, test with historical data, and produce the configuration document.

steps.description: Select the business metrics to monitor with threshold alerts.

inputs.name: business-kpis
inputs.desc: List of business KPIs and operational metrics

inputs.name: historical-metric-data
inputs.desc: Historical data for the candidate metrics (last 30 to 90 days)

outputs.name: selected-metrics
outputs.desc: Metrics selected for threshold alerting with rationale

outputs.name: baseline-values
outputs.desc: Baseline values (mean, standard deviation, percentiles) for each selected metric

process: Review the business KPIs and select those where a deviation requires immediate human attention.
For each selected metric, pull 30 to 90 days of historical data.
Calculate the baseline: mean, standard deviation, p5, p50, p95.
Exclude metrics that are too noisy or too stable for threshold alerting.

steps.description: Set the thresholds for each metric: static, dynamic, or anomaly-based.

outputs.name: threshold-rules
outputs.desc: Threshold rules for each metric (type, value, evaluation window)

outputs.name: alert-channels
outputs.desc: Channel and recipient assignment for each threshold alert

process: For each metric, choose the threshold type: static (fixed value), dynamic (percentage deviation from rolling average), or anomaly-based (standard deviations from baseline).
Set the threshold value based on the baseline statistics and acceptable tolerance.
Define the evaluation window (e.g., 5-minute average, 15-minute sum).
Assign each alert to a channel and recipient based on the metric's domain (revenue alerts to finance, error rates to engineering).

steps.description: Set cool-down periods and deduplication rules to prevent alert storms.

outputs.name: cooldown-config
outputs.desc: Cool-down period and deduplication rules for each alert

outputs.name: grouping-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for grouping related alerts into a single notification

process: Set a cool-down period for each alert (e.g., do not re-fire for 30 minutes after the last fire).
Configure deduplication so identical alerts within the cool-down window are suppressed.
Define grouping rules for related metrics (e.g., if both error rate and latency breach, send one grouped alert).
Document the rationale for each cool-down setting.

steps.description: Test the thresholds against historical data and produce the configuration document.

outputs.name: backtest-results
outputs.desc: Results of running the thresholds against historical data (fires, false positives, missed events)

outputs.name: threshold-configuration-document
outputs.desc: Final configuration document with all metrics, thresholds, channels, and cool-down settings

process: Run each threshold rule against the historical data to see how many times it would have fired.
Compare the fires against known incidents to calculate the true positive and false positive rates.
Adjust any thresholds that produce too many false positives or miss known incidents.
Compile the final configuration document with all settings, backtest results, and the tuning rationale.
